$comment: Third-party agent skills. 'vendored' entries are copied verbatim into vendor/skills/<id>/ with their upstream LICENSE and are installed alongside the framework skills. 'referenced' entries are not redistributed; install them from upstream with the listed command.

vendored.name: Fixing Accessibility
vendored.summary: Audit and fix accessible names, keyboard access, focus and dialogs, semantics, form errors, announcements and contrast. Reports violations with a minimal code fix.

vendored.name: Fixing Motion Performance
vendored.summary: Audit animation cost: compositor-only properties, layout thrashing, scroll-linked motion, blur and layer promotion.

vendored.name: Design Engineering (Emil Kowalski)
vendored.summary: Animation decision framework (whether, why, easing, duration), component polish rules, transform and clip-path techniques, and a review format.

vendored.name: Review Animations (Emil Kowalski)
vendored.summary: Strict review of motion code against a written standard. Flags by default; approval has to be earned.

vendored.name: Ponytail (smallest complete change)
vendored.summary: Write the least new code that fully solves the task: reuse what exists, prefer the standard library, finish every caller and test the change breaks, and never cut validation, security or accessibility.

vendored.name: Ponytail Review
vendored.summary: Review a change for correctness, safety, load, tests, speed and lean code. Every finding needs a concrete failing case and comes with the smallest fix.

vendored.name: Ponytail Audit
vendored.summary: Audit a whole repository the same way: bugs, security, scale, missing tests, slow paths and what to delete, merge or split, ranked and explained.

vendored.name: Grilling (Matt Pocock)
vendored.summary: Interview the user in rounds over a design tree, each question with a recommended answer, until every decision is settled and nothing is silently assumed.

vendored.name: Domain Modeling (Matt Pocock)
vendored.summary: Keep a shared glossary and architecture decision records so the words in conversations, specs and code mean the same thing.

vendored.name: Test-Driven Development (Matt Pocock)
vendored.summary: Red, green, refactor at the highest useful seam; test behaviour, not implementation, and mock only at system boundaries.

referenced.name: Web Interface Guidelines (Vercel)
referenced.reasonNotVendored: No license file detected in the upstream repository, so it is not redistributed.
referenced.summary: Review UI code for accessibility, keyboard support, forms, animation and performance, reported as file:line findings.

referenced.name: Frontend Design (Anthropic)
referenced.reasonNotVendored: No repository-level license detected; installed from upstream instead.
referenced.summary: A design-thinking step before code: purpose, audience, a deliberate tone, and a list of generic defaults to avoid.

referenced.name: Impeccable (Paul Bakaus)
referenced.reasonNotVendored: Apache-2.0, but the skill depends on many reference files and per-tool variants; installing upstream keeps it intact and current.
referenced.summary: A command sequence for design work: audit, arrange, typeset, polish.

referenced.name: Baseline UI (ibelick, upstream)
referenced.reasonNotVendored: The framework ships its own skills/baseline-ui adapted to plain CSS tokens; the upstream version assumes Tailwind and motion/react.
referenced.summary: Opinionated constraints against generic AI UI: no gradients or glows, one accent per view, compositor-only animation.

referenced.name: Anthony Fu skills collection
referenced.reasonNotVendored: Framework-specific (Vue, Nuxt, Vite, Vitest, UnoCSS). Install only in projects that use that stack.
referenced.summary: Conventions for antfu, antfu-create-pr, nitro, nuxt, pinia, pnpm, unocss, vite, vitepress, vitest and vue.

referenced.name: To Spec (Matt Pocock)
referenced.reasonNotVendored: Publishes to an issue tracker configured by /setup-matt-pocock-skills, which is not part of this framework. The idea-to-prd skill writes the same kind of spec to a local file instead.
referenced.summary: Turn a settled conversation into a spec: problem, solution, numbered user stories, implementation and testing decisions, out of scope.

referenced.name: To Tickets (Matt Pocock)
referenced.reasonNotVendored: Depends on the same tracker setup. idea-to-prd covers vertical, tracer-bullet tickets written to local files.
referenced.summary: Break a spec into vertical, demoable tickets with blocking edges, including expand-and-contract for wide refactors.

referenced.name: Code Review (Matt Pocock)
referenced.reasonNotVendored: Expects the tracker setup to find the originating spec. The code-reviewer agent uses ponytail-review and independent-review, which need no setup.
referenced.summary: Two-axis review in parallel sub-agents: repository standards (with a code-smell baseline) and fidelity to the originating spec.
